label: Moral supervenience comparison profile
definition: A Profile has an admitted situation type World, a shared case type Case, Boolean selected nonmoral profile values, alleged moral fact statuses, one verdict function per world and a separate world-competence predicate. The World carrier selects what situations are under comparison; no appraiser identity, entire metaphysical possibility space, identity through worlds, or complete nature-description is certified.
note: Analyst structural fixture, attribution deferred. As an analogy outside this single-verdict-per-world signature, two appraisers might disagree about naturally identical cases without any corresponding moral-fact difference. Conversely selecting an incomplete base can create spurious supervenience failures. The real-world coverage and completeness of the natural profile, interpretation of case identities and connection of verdicts to moral truth remain OPEN. Serves the moral-grounding rival question (#150/#249) and the Blackburn competence question (#191), not a new direct root proof.
